newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest grains go limit-down, fall seen slowing.
newsitem.headline: Budapest grains go limit-down, fall seen slowing.

text.p: Good international crop forecasts and favourable weather pushed most grains futures prices of the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) limit-down and the falling trend was seen continuing, traders said on Monday.
"Prices will probably fall further, although at a slowing pace," said Istvan Markus of Swap brokerage.
He added said that with the Chicago market closed on Monday, Tuesday's Hungarian market will receive less outside information for guidance.
On Monday, milling wheat futures went down the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne for all but July, to end at 23,300 forints for August, 24,500 for December and 26,500 for May.

However, maize prices did not reflect current, ideal weather conditions. July rose went limit-up to end at 20,400 forints, October remained flat at 19,710 forints and prices dropped for further maturities between 50 forints for November and 400 for each of May and July 1998.
"July (1997) prices rose mainly because one player bought everything on offer," Markus said.

Barley and feed wheat prices went limit-down, mirroring milling wheat price changes but turnover remained low for all but July maize and October milling wheat, which, between them, accounted for one quarter of the day's turnover in volume terms.
The BCE's grains futures turnover edged up to 380.2 million forints or 844 from 342 million forints or 673 lots on Friday.
